name: High-Use Chronic Pharmacology Intelligence Labs
global_boundary: Research/learning classification atlas only. Typical adult dose snapshots are educational references, not patient-specific prescriptions. Verify diagnosis, formulation, current approved label/guideline, age/weight, renal/hepatic function, pregnancy/lactation, contraindications, interactions and monitoring before prescribing.

labs.title: Antihypertensive Intelligence Lab
labs.subtitle: Classification → RAAS / CCB / diuretics / sympathetic systems → generics → dose/formulation → compelling-context lens → evidence verification
labs.scientific_boundary: This is a pharmacology/research atlas, not an automatic antihypertensive selector. “First-line/core”, CKD, pregnancy, resistant-HTN and emergency tags are learning/context lenses. Actual choice requires confirmed BP phenotype, comorbidities, kidney function/electrolytes, pregnancy status, interactions and the current guideline/label.

classification_notes.first_line: 2025 AHA/ACC identifies ACE inhibitors, ARBs, long-acting dihydropyridine CCBs and thiazide-type diuretics as major classes used to initiate treatment; individualized combinations and comorbidities determine selection.
classification_notes.raas: ACEi and ARB are alternative RAAS-blocking strategies; routine dual RAAS blockade is generally avoided because of renal/hyperkalemia risk.
classification_notes.resistant: Resistant hypertension requires confirmation of adherence/measurement, secondary-cause review and rational combination therapy; MRA therapy is a key pharmacologic teaching category.
classification_notes.emergency: Hypertensive emergency is defined by severe BP elevation with acute target-organ injury; IV agent choice and rate of BP reduction are syndrome-specific and monitored-setting decisions.

classes.name: ACE inhibitors (ACEi)
classes.mechanism: Reduce angiotensin II formation and bradykinin breakdown
classes.role_note: Core RAAS-blocking class; common foundational option when indicated. ACEi and ARB should not be combined routinely.

classes.name: Angiotensin II receptor blockers (ARB)
classes.mechanism: Block angiotensin II signaling at AT1 receptor
classes.role_note: Core RAAS-blocking class; often used when ACEi cough/angioedema context makes ACEi unsuitable.

classes.name: Long-acting dihydropyridine CCBs
classes.mechanism: Reduce vascular smooth-muscle calcium entry and arteriolar resistance
classes.role_note: Core BP-lowering class with strong vasodilator effect; edema is a common class effect.

classes.name: Non-dihydropyridine CCBs
classes.mechanism: Reduce AV-node conduction and myocardial/vascular calcium entry
classes.role_note: Useful when rate control is also desired; not interchangeable with DHP-CCBs.

classes.name: Thiazide / thiazide-like diuretics
classes.mechanism: Promote natriuresis at distal convoluted tubule
classes.role_note: Core hypertension class; chlorthalidone/indapamide are longer acting thiazide-like options.

classes.name: Loop diuretics
classes.mechanism: Potent natriuresis in thick ascending limb
classes.role_note: More useful for volume overload/heart failure/advanced CKD than uncomplicated hypertension.

classes.name: Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists
classes.mechanism: Block aldosterone signaling and sodium retention
classes.role_note: High-yield add-on class in resistant hypertension and selected heart-failure contexts; potassium/renal monitoring is central.

classes.name: Epithelial sodium-channel blockers
classes.mechanism: Reduce sodium reabsorption in collecting duct
classes.role_note: Potassium-sparing diuretics; usually adjunctive rather than first-line monotherapy.

classes.name: β1-selective beta blockers
classes.mechanism: Reduce heart rate, contractility and renin release
classes.role_note: Not universal first-line hypertension therapy, but important with CAD/post-MI, tachyarrhythmia and selected HF contexts.

classes.name: Combined α/β blockers
classes.mechanism: Reduce sympathetic vascular tone and cardiac adrenergic drive
classes.role_note: Labetalol is important in pregnancy/emergency contexts; carvedilol is a heart-failure/CAD drug with BP effects.

classes.name: Non-selective beta blockers
classes.mechanism: Block β1 and β2 adrenergic receptors
classes.role_note: Useful for selected compelling indications; bronchospasm risk matters.

classes.name: α1-adrenergic blockers
classes.mechanism: Reduce peripheral vascular α1-mediated tone
classes.role_note: Usually add-on therapy; can help concomitant BPH but orthostatic hypotension is important.

classes.name: Central sympatholytics / α2 agonists
classes.mechanism: Reduce central sympathetic outflow
classes.role_note: Generally later-line; rebound hypertension is important with abrupt clonidine withdrawal.

classes.name: Direct arteriolar vasodilators
classes.mechanism: Directly relax arteriolar smooth muscle
classes.role_note: Hydralazine/minoxidil are later-line agents; reflex tachycardia and fluid retention often require companion therapy.

classes.name: Direct renin inhibitor
classes.mechanism: Suppresses RAAS at renin step
classes.role_note: Aliskiren is a specialist/alternative RAAS agent; combination restrictions with ACEi/ARB are important in selected populations.

classes.name: Angiotensin receptor–neprilysin inhibitor (ARNI)
classes.mechanism: AT1 blockade plus neprilysin inhibition
classes.role_note: Primarily a heart-failure therapy with BP-lowering effect; not a routine hypertension-first-line class.

classes.name: IV antihypertensive / hypertensive-emergency agents
classes.mechanism: Rapid titratable hemodynamic control in monitored settings
classes.role_note: Hospital/ICU category only. Agent choice depends on acute target-organ injury, aortic syndrome, ACS, pregnancy, pulmonary edema, renal function and local protocol.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult HTN start: 25 mg twice daily; titrate to response.
drugs.role: Short acting ACEi; useful when rapid oral titration is desired.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: BP, creatinine/eGFR and potassium; cough/angioedema teaching point.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult HTN start: 5 mg once daily; usual total 10–40 mg/day.
drugs.role: Widely used ACEi; enalaprilat is the IV active metabolite.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: BP, creatinine/eGFR and potassium; cough/angioedema teaching point.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult HTN start: 10 mg once daily; usual 10–40 mg/day.
drugs.role: Once-daily ACEi with broad cardiovascular use.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: BP, creatinine/eGFR and potassium; cough/angioedema teaching point.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult HTN start: 2.5 mg once daily; usual 2.5–10 mg/day.
drugs.role: Common cardioprotective ACEi in CAD/high-risk contexts.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: BP, creatinine/eGFR and potassium; cough/angioedema teaching point.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult HTN start: 4 mg once daily; usual 4–8 mg/day (salt/formulation dependent).
drugs.role: Long-acting ACEi; formulation salts vary by market.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: BP, creatinine/eGFR and potassium; cough/angioedema teaching point.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult HTN start: 10 mg once daily; usual 10–40 mg/day.
drugs.role: Long-acting ACEi.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: BP, creatinine/eGFR and potassium; cough/angioedema teaching point.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult HTN start: 10 mg once daily; usual 10–40 mg/day.
drugs.role: Mixed renal/hepatic elimination is a pharmacokinetic teaching point.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: BP, creatinine/eGFR and potassium; cough/angioedema teaching point.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult HTN start: 10–20 mg/day; titrate per label/response.
drugs.role: Availability varies by jurisdiction.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: BP, creatinine/eGFR and potassium; cough/angioedema teaching point.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult HTN start: 1 mg once daily; usual 1–4 mg/day.

drugs.dose_example: Common HTN start 40 mg once daily; range 20–80 mg/day.
drugs.role: AT1-selective RAAS blockade; verify indication and renal/potassium context.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: BP, creatinine/eGFR and potassium.

drugs.dose_example: Common HTN start 20 mg once daily; range 20–40 mg/day.
drugs.role: AT1-selective RAAS blockade; verify indication and renal/potassium context.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: BP, creatinine/eGFR and potassium.

drugs.dose_example: Common HTN start 150 mg once daily; range 150–300 mg/day.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult start 30–60 mg once daily; formulation-specific maximum varies.
drugs.role: Predominantly vascular L-type calcium-channel blockade.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: BP, ankle edema, flushing/headache; formulation-specific interactions.

drugs.role: Rate-slowing CCB with stronger AV-node effect.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: BP, HR/ECG, constipation and interaction review.

drugs.dose_example: 12.5–25 mg once daily is a common HTN range.
drugs.role: NCC blockade lowers sodium balance and peripheral resistance over time.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: BP, sodium, potassium, uric acid, renal function and volume status.

drugs.dose_example: 1.25–2.5 mg once daily is a common HTN range.
drugs.role: NCC blockade lowers sodium balance and peripheral resistance over time.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: BP, sodium, potassium, uric acid, renal function and volume status.

drugs.monitoring_pearl: BP, sodium, potassium, uric acid, renal function and volume status.

drugs.dose_example: 2.5–5 mg once daily is often used for diuretic-resistant edema; not routine uncomplicated HTN first-line.
drugs.role: NCC blockade lowers sodium balance and peripheral resistance over time.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: BP, sodium, potassium, uric acid, renal function and volume status.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult oral start 20–40 mg; dose/frequency highly volume- and kidney-dependent.
drugs.role: Potent loop diuresis; BP effect is often secondary to volume management.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult edema/HTN start 5–10 mg once daily; higher doses for congestion.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult oral start 25–50 mg/day; specialist use, especially when sulfonamide-loop avoidance is needed.
drugs.role: Potent loop diuresis; BP effect is often secondary to volume management.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Volume status, BP, sodium/potassium/magnesium, renal function.

drugs.dose_example: Common resistant-HTN start 12.5–25 mg once daily; often 25–50 mg/day.
drugs.role: Aldosterone blockade; strong resistant-HTN teaching class.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Potassium and renal function are mandatory; endocrine adverse effects differ between agents.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult start 25–50 mg once daily; may require twice-daily dosing by indication.
drugs.role: Aldosterone blockade; strong resistant-HTN teaching class.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Potassium and renal function are mandatory; endocrine adverse effects differ between agents.

drugs.monitoring_pearl: Potassium, renal function and volume status.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult dosing 50–100 mg once or twice daily depending formulation/combo.
drugs.role: Potassium-sparing ENaC blockade.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Potassium and renal function.

drugs.role: β1 blockade lowers HR/contractility/renin; compelling indications often determine use.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: BP, heart rate, conduction, bronchospasm/metabolic masking considerations.

drugs.dose_example: 2.5–5 mg once daily is a common start; usual HTN range 2.5–10 mg/day.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult start 200 mg twice daily; titrate by response.
drugs.role: β1 blockade lowers HR/contractility/renin; compelling indications often determine use.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: BP, heart rate, conduction, bronchospasm/metabolic masking considerations.

drugs.dose_example: Oral HTN often starts 100 mg twice daily; IV regimens are monitored-setting and protocol-specific.

drugs.monitoring_pearl: BP/HR; IV use requires monitored titration.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult start 3.125–6.25 mg twice daily in HF or 6.25–12.5 mg twice daily in HTN; titrate slowly.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult HTN start 40 mg twice daily; dose depends strongly on indication/formulation.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult start 40 mg once daily; titrate by indication/renal function.
drugs.role: Long-acting nonselective beta blocker.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: BP/HR and renal dose review.

drugs.dose_example: 1 mg two or three times daily is a common cautious start; first-dose syncope risk.
drugs.role: α1 blockade lowers vascular tone and can improve BPH symptoms.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Orthostatic BP and falls risk.

drugs.dose_example: 1 mg once daily is a common start; titrate gradually.
drugs.role: α1 blockade lowers vascular tone and can improve BPH symptoms.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Orthostatic BP and falls risk.

drugs.dose_example: 1 mg at bedtime is a common start; titrate gradually.
drugs.role: α1 blockade lowers vascular tone and can improve BPH symptoms.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Orthostatic BP and falls risk.

drugs.dose_example: Common oral start 0.1 mg twice daily; transdermal systems are weekly and strength-specific.
drugs.role: Central sympatholytic; abrupt withdrawal may cause rebound hypertension.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: BP/HR, sedation, adherence and tapering plan.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult start 250 mg two or three times daily; pregnancy use follows obstetric guidance.
drugs.role: Historic/important pregnancy-context antihypertensive.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: BP, sedation; long-term liver/CBC monitoring per context.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult HTN start historically 1 mg once daily at bedtime; current availability/indication varies.
drugs.role: Long-acting central α2 agonist; more commonly encountered in ADHD care today.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: BP/HR and sedation.

drugs.dose_example: Oral HTN often starts 10–25 mg two to four times daily; IV use is protocol-specific.
drugs.role: Direct arteriolar dilator; often paired with beta blocker/diuretic in chronic use.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: BP/HR, edema; lupus-like syndrome with prolonged/high exposure.

drugs.dose_example: Common specialist start 2.5–5 mg once daily; titrate cautiously for refractory HTN.
drugs.role: Very potent arteriolar dilator reserved for refractory hypertension.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: BP, pulse, edema/weight; usually needs loop diuretic + beta blocker.

drugs.dose_example: 150 mg once daily is a common adult start; may increase to 300 mg/day.
drugs.role: Direct renin inhibition.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: BP, renal function, potassium; RAAS-combination restrictions.

drugs.dose_example: HF dosing is strength- and prior-RAAS-therapy dependent; commonly initiated twice daily. Verify exact product label.
drugs.role: Primarily HFrEF/selected HF therapy, not routine hypertension monotherapy.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: BP, potassium, renal function; ACEi washout requirement.

drugs.dose_example: Common ICU start 5 mg/hour, titrated in small increments per protocol.
drugs.role: Titrated arterial vasodilation. Not for routine outpatient hypertension.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Continuous/very frequent BP; agent-specific hemodynamic, renal/metabolic and toxicity monitoring.

drugs.dose_example: Common ICU start 1–2 mg/hour with rapid titration per protocol.
drugs.role: Ultra-short DHP vasodilation. Not for routine outpatient hypertension.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Continuous/very frequent BP; agent-specific hemodynamic, renal/metabolic and toxicity monitoring.

drugs.dose_example: Example bolus 20 mg IV then repeat/escalate or infusion per monitored protocol.
drugs.role: α/β blockade. Not for routine outpatient hypertension.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Continuous/very frequent BP; agent-specific hemodynamic, renal/metabolic and toxicity monitoring.

drugs.dose_example: Loading/infusion is weight-based; common maintenance starts around 50 microgram/kg/min.
drugs.role: Ultra-short β1 blockade. Not for routine outpatient hypertension.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Continuous/very frequent BP; agent-specific hemodynamic, renal/metabolic and toxicity monitoring.

drugs.dose_example: Common ICU start ~0.3 microgram/kg/min and titrate; toxicity limits require strict monitoring.
drugs.role: NO-mediated arterial/venous dilation. Not for routine outpatient hypertension.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Continuous/very frequent BP; agent-specific hemodynamic, renal/metabolic and toxicity monitoring.

drugs.dose_example: Common monitored start 5 microgram/min and titrate; especially useful with ACS/pulmonary edema contexts.
drugs.role: Predominantly venodilation at lower doses. Not for routine outpatient hypertension.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Continuous/very frequent BP; agent-specific hemodynamic, renal/metabolic and toxicity monitoring.

drugs.dose_example: Common bolus examples 5–10 mg IV; repeat per protocol and pregnancy context.
drugs.role: Direct arteriolar dilation. Not for routine outpatient hypertension.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Continuous/very frequent BP; agent-specific hemodynamic, renal/metabolic and toxicity monitoring.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult IV example 1.25 mg every 6 hours; selected settings only.
drugs.role: IV ACE inhibition. Not for routine outpatient hypertension.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Continuous/very frequent BP; agent-specific hemodynamic, renal/metabolic and toxicity monitoring.

drugs.dose_example: Common ICU start 0.1 microgram/kg/min and titrate.
drugs.role: D1-receptor agonist vasodilation. Not for routine outpatient hypertension.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Continuous/very frequent BP; agent-specific hemodynamic, renal/metabolic and toxicity monitoring.

labs.title: Antidiabetic Intelligence Lab
labs.subtitle: Classification → glucose physiology target → oral/injectable/insulin families → generics/formulations → cardiorenal/weight lenses → evidence verification
labs.scientific_boundary: This lab is a pharmacology and evidence-navigation workspace, not an automatic glucose-lowering regimen generator. Comorbidity lenses (ASCVD, HF, CKD, weight, hypoglycemia) are research prompts; treatment must integrate diabetes type, HbA1c/glucose pattern, symptoms, renal/hepatic function, pregnancy, age/frailty, cost/access and current label/guideline.

classification_notes.physiology: Drug classes can be understood by dominant physiology: hepatic glucose output/insulin sensitivity, pancreatic insulin secretion, incretin signaling, renal glucose transport, intestinal carbohydrate absorption and exogenous insulin replacement.
classification_notes.cardiorenal: Modern T2D therapy is not ranked only by HbA1c. SGLT2 inhibitors and selected GLP-1–based therapies have important cardiorenal/weight roles in appropriate patients.
classification_notes.insulin: Insulin is mandatory replacement in type 1 diabetes and may be needed in type 2 diabetes for marked hyperglycemia, catabolic symptoms, acute illness or progressive beta-cell failure.
classification_notes.hypoglycemia: Insulin and secretagogues carry greater hypoglycemia risk than metformin, SGLT2 inhibitors, DPP-4 inhibitors, TZDs and GLP-1–based therapies when used without insulin/secretagogue.

classes.name: Biguanide
classes.mechanism: Suppresses hepatic glucose production and improves insulin sensitivity
classes.role_note: Metformin-centered foundational class in many T2D pathways; renal tolerance and GI/B12 issues matter.

classes.name: Sulfonylureas
classes.mechanism: Close β-cell KATP channels → insulin release
classes.role_note: Potent, inexpensive insulin secretagogues; hypoglycemia and weight gain are major selection trade-offs.

classes.name: Meglitinides / glinides
classes.mechanism: Short-acting KATP-channel closure → meal-time insulin release
classes.role_note: Meal-time secretagogues with shorter action than sulfonylureas.

classes.name: Thiazolidinediones (TZD)
classes.mechanism: Increase insulin sensitivity through nuclear transcription effects
classes.role_note: Insulin-sensitizing class; edema/HF, fractures and weight effects shape use.

classes.name: α-glucosidase inhibitors
classes.mechanism: Delay intestinal carbohydrate digestion/absorption
classes.role_note: Postprandial-focused agents; gastrointestinal adverse effects are common.

classes.name: DPP-4 inhibitors (gliptins)
classes.mechanism: Prolong endogenous GLP-1/GIP action
classes.role_note: Generally weight-neutral, low-hypoglycemia oral incretin enhancers; renal dosing differs by molecule.

classes.name: SGLT2 inhibitors
classes.mechanism: Increase urinary glucose excretion and alter renal-cardiorenal physiology
classes.role_note: Glucose-lowering plus important HF/CKD benefits for selected patients; eGFR and acute illness/ketosis precautions matter.

classes.name: Dual SGLT1/SGLT2 inhibitor
classes.mechanism: Reduces intestinal glucose absorption and renal glucose reabsorption
classes.role_note: Specialized dual transporter inhibition; regulatory indications vary by country.

classes.name: GLP-1 receptor agonists
classes.mechanism: Enhance glucose-dependent insulin secretion, suppress glucagon, slow gastric emptying and increase satiety
classes.role_note: High-efficacy incretin class with substantial weight and cardiometabolic effects depending agent.

classes.name: Dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist
classes.mechanism: Dual incretin-receptor agonism
classes.role_note: Very high glycemic and weight efficacy; GI effects and titration are central.

classes.name: Amylin analog
classes.mechanism: Slows gastric emptying, suppresses postprandial glucagon and increases satiety
classes.role_note: Adjunct to mealtime insulin in selected patients; insulin-dose coordination is essential.

classes.name: Other oral glucose-lowering agents
classes.mechanism: Miscellaneous central/bile-acid/mitochondrial mechanisms
classes.role_note: Less commonly used/region-specific oral agents that remain pharmacologically relevant.

classes.name: Rapid / ultra-rapid insulin analogs
classes.mechanism: Exogenous insulin replacement with rapid prandial kinetics
classes.role_note: Prandial insulin category; dosing is carbohydrate/glucose/insulin-sensitivity dependent rather than a universal fixed dose.

classes.name: Short-acting human insulin
classes.mechanism: Exogenous insulin replacement with slower prandial kinetics than analogs
classes.role_note: Regular human insulin; also used IV in specific acute-care protocols.

classes.name: Intermediate-acting insulin
classes.mechanism: Basal/intermediate insulin replacement
classes.role_note: NPH has pronounced peak and more hypoglycemia variability than long-acting analogs.

classes.name: Long / ultra-long basal insulin analogs
classes.mechanism: Relatively peakless basal insulin replacement
classes.role_note: Basal insulin category for T1D and advanced T2D; titration is individualized.

classes.name: Premixed insulin formulations
classes.mechanism: Fixed basal/prandial insulin proportions
classes.role_note: Simplifies injection schedule but reduces flexibility; meal consistency matters.

classes.name: Fixed-dose / fixed-ratio diabetes combinations
classes.mechanism: Combines complementary pharmacologic pathways
classes.role_note: Common combination patterns can reduce pill/injection burden; exact strength and suitability are product-specific.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult start 500 mg once or twice daily with food; titrate gradually.
drugs.role: Foundational T2D medicine in many algorithms.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: HbA1c/glucose, eGFR; B12 with long-term use.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult start 500 mg once daily with evening meal; titrate by tolerance/label.
drugs.role: Same pharmacology with slower release and often better GI tolerability.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: HbA1c/glucose, eGFR; B12 long-term.

drugs.dose_example: 1–2 mg once daily with breakfast/first meal.
drugs.role: KATP-dependent insulin secretagogue; effectiveness requires residual β-cell function.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Glucose/HbA1c; hypoglycemia and weight.

drugs.dose_example: 30 mg once daily with breakfast is a common start where licensed.
drugs.role: KATP-dependent insulin secretagogue; effectiveness requires residual β-cell function.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Glucose/HbA1c; hypoglycemia and weight.

drugs.dose_example: 2.5–5 mg once daily ~30 min before breakfast is a common start.
drugs.role: KATP-dependent insulin secretagogue; effectiveness requires residual β-cell function.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Glucose/HbA1c; hypoglycemia and weight.

labs.title: Thyroid Drugs Intelligence Lab
labs.subtitle: Hypothyroid replacement → hyperthyroid synthesis/release blockers → symptom control → thyroid storm → radioiodine → orbitopathy → precision oncology
labs.scientific_boundary: This lab separates thyroid pharmacology by disease mechanism. Replacement, antithyroid, thyroid-storm, pregnancy, orbitopathy and oncology therapies are not interchangeable. Exact drug choice/dose must be based on thyroid diagnosis, TSH/free T4/T3 pattern, etiology (Graves/toxic nodule/thyroiditis), pregnancy status, cardiac/liver risk and current ATA/product guidance.

classification_notes.hypothyroid: Levothyroxine remains standard replacement for primary hypothyroidism; dose is individualized by age, weight, pregnancy, cardiac disease and TSH response.
classification_notes.hyperthyroid: Thionamides block new hormone synthesis and are useful in Graves disease; they do not treat hormone leakage from thyroiditis. Beta blockers control symptoms but do not correct hormone production.
classification_notes.storm: Thyroid storm is a multimodal emergency: adrenergic control + synthesis blockade + iodide after thionamide + glucocorticoid/supportive care, with syndrome-specific protocol.
classification_notes.pregnancy: Pregnancy management is specialized. ATA updated its preconception/pregnancy/postpartum guideline in 2026; antithyroid and levothyroxine decisions should use that current guidance.

classes.name: T4 replacement
classes.mechanism: Replaces endogenous thyroxine; peripheral conversion supplies T3
classes.target: Thyroid hormone receptors after T4→T3 conversion
classes.role_note: Levothyroxine is standard replacement therapy for primary hypothyroidism; dose is TSH/clinical-context guided.

classes.name: T3 / combination thyroid hormone
classes.mechanism: Provides liothyronine directly or T4/T3 combination
classes.role_note: Specialist/selected use rather than routine first-line replacement.

classes.name: Desiccated thyroid extract
classes.mechanism: Animal-derived T4/T3-containing preparation
classes.role_note: Not standard first-line therapy; content ratio differs from human physiology and products require careful standardization.

classes.name: Thionamide antithyroid drugs
classes.mechanism: Inhibit thyroid peroxidase; PTU also reduces peripheral T4→T3 conversion
classes.role_note: Core medication class for Graves hyperthyroidism; methimazole is usually preferred outside specific pregnancy/thyroid-storm contexts.

classes.name: Beta blockers for thyrotoxicosis
classes.mechanism: Control adrenergic symptoms; propranolol at higher doses also reduces T4→T3 conversion
classes.role_note: Symptom-control adjunct; does not treat the underlying hormone overproduction.

classes.name: Inorganic iodide / hormone-release blockade
classes.mechanism: Acute Wolff–Chaikoff effect and inhibition of thyroid hormone release
classes.role_note: Short-term adjunct in thyroid storm/preoperative settings; sequencing after thionamide matters in storm protocols.

classes.name: Radioactive iodine (I-131)
classes.mechanism: Thyroid-selective beta radiation after iodide uptake
classes.role_note: Definitive therapy for selected Graves/toxic nodular disease; contraindications and radiation precautions are essential.

classes.name: Thyroid-storm / severe thyrotoxicosis adjuncts
classes.mechanism: Reduce peripheral conversion, enterohepatic recycling or hormone release
classes.role_note: ICU-level multimodal therapy; components are adjuncts and sequence/timing are protocol-driven.

classes.name: Graves orbitopathy pharmacotherapy
classes.mechanism: Immunomodulation / IGF-1R pathway inhibition
classes.role_note: Specialist ophthalmology/endocrinology therapy based on activity/severity and local availability.

classes.name: Rare/specialist hormone-release inhibitors
classes.mechanism: Reduce thyroid hormone release/iodide uptake in selected refractory or amiodarone contexts
classes.role_note: Rare specialist agents; toxicity and availability limit routine use.

classes.name: RAI-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer targeted therapy
classes.mechanism: Inhibit VEGFR/RET and other oncogenic kinases
classes.role_note: Oncology-level systemic therapy for progressive RAI-refractory disease; mutation and toxicity profiles guide selection.

classes.name: Medullary thyroid cancer targeted therapy
classes.mechanism: Inhibit RET/VEGFR/MET or selective RET signaling
classes.role_note: Advanced medullary thyroid cancer therapy; RET mutation status increasingly matters.

classes.name: Anaplastic thyroid cancer / precision therapy
classes.mechanism: Target BRAF/MEK or actionable molecular drivers
classes.role_note: Urgent multidisciplinary oncology care; targeted options depend on rapid molecular profiling.

drugs.dose_example: Healthy younger adults needing full replacement often require ~1.6 microgram/kg/day; start lower in older/cardiac patients and titrate by TSH.
drugs.role: Standard of care for hypothyroidism.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: TSH (and free T4 in selected contexts), adherence/timing; absorption interactions with iron/calcium/antacids.

drugs.dose_example: Dose is microgram-for-microgram individualized similarly to tablet; formulation changes should be followed by thyroid-function reassessment.
drugs.role: Alternative formulation for selected absorption/excipient issues.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: TSH after formulation/dose change.

drugs.dose_example: Individualized microgram dose; verify product concentration and administration instructions.
drugs.role: Liquid formulation may be useful for swallowing/absorption situations.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: TSH and exact concentration verification.

drugs.dose_example: Label oral starting doses are commonly around 25 microgram/day in adults, much lower in older/cardiac patients; specialist titration is essential.
drugs.role: Short-acting T3; not routine monotherapy for primary hypothyroidism.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: TSH/free T4/T3 as appropriate, HR/arrhythmia and symptoms.

drugs.dose_example: No universal fixed ratio/dose; specialist protocols individualize LT4 reduction and small LT3 doses.
drugs.role: Selected trial only after confirming diagnosis/adherence and persistent symptoms; not routine standard care.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: TSH, symptoms, HR; avoid supraphysiologic T3 exposure.

drugs.dose_example: Product is standardized in mg/grain units; conversion to physiologic LT4-equivalent is not exact. Verify product-specific labeling.
drugs.role: Contains fixed T4:T3 ratio; not standard first-line therapy.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: TSH and symptoms; avoid T3 excess.

drugs.dose_example: Initial dose depends on free T4/T3 severity; common adult starts range roughly 5–20 mg/day, with higher doses for marked thyrotoxicosis.
drugs.role: Preferred thionamide for most nonpregnant Graves patients.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Free T4/T3 and TSH over time; counsel urgently for fever/sore throat and hepatic symptoms.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult initial total dose 15–40 mg/day in divided doses where licensed; maintenance is much lower and lab-guided.
drugs.role: Prodrug converted to methimazole; widely used in India/UK and other markets.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Thyroid function; agranulocytosis/hepatic symptom counseling.

drugs.dose_example: Common adult initial 50–150 mg three times daily depending severity; thyroid-storm regimens are higher/protocol-specific.
drugs.role: Generally reserved for first-trimester pregnancy, thyroid storm or selected intolerance because of serious hepatic risk.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Thyroid function; hepatic symptoms/LFT context; agranulocytosis counseling.

drugs.dose_example: 20–40 mg every 6–8 h is a common symptom-control range; higher storm dosing is protocol-specific.
drugs.role: Controls tremor, palpitations and tachycardia; propranolol has additional peripheral-conversion effect at higher doses.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Heart rate/BP; bronchospasm/conduction context.

drugs.dose_example: 25–50 mg once daily is a common symptom-control start.
drugs.role: Controls tremor, palpitations and tachycardia; propranolol has additional peripheral-conversion effect at higher doses.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Heart rate/BP; bronchospasm/conduction context.

drugs.dose_example: 25–50 mg twice daily (tartrate) or ER equivalent is commonly used for symptom control.
drugs.role: Controls tremor, palpitations and tachycardia; propranolol has additional peripheral-conversion effect at higher doses.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Heart rate/BP; bronchospasm/conduction context.

drugs.dose_example: Weight-based ICU infusion; useful when very rapid titration is needed.
drugs.role: Controls tremor, palpitations and tachycardia; propranolol has additional peripheral-conversion effect at higher doses.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Heart rate/BP; bronchospasm/conduction context.

drugs.dose_example: Preparation concentrations vary; dosing is in drops/mg and must be verified from exact product/protocol. In storm, iodide is generally given after thionamide.
drugs.role: Rapid short-term blockade of hormone release/organification.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Thyroid function, iodism/allergy and exact concentration.

drugs.dose_example: Exact drop concentration varies by preparation; use only with verified protocol/product.
drugs.role: Short-term iodide strategy; not long-term antithyroid monotherapy.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Exact concentration and thyroid function.

drugs.dose_example: Activity is individualized by indication, gland characteristics and nuclear-medicine protocol; no universal fixed dose.
drugs.role: Definitive ablation for selected hyperthyroidism/thyroid cancer indications.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Pregnancy exclusion, radiation precautions and follow-up thyroid function.

drugs.dose_example: A common thyroid-storm regimen is 100 mg IV every 8 hours; verify ICU protocol.
drugs.role: Reduces peripheral T4→T3 conversion and treats possible relative adrenal insufficiency.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Glucose, infection, hemodynamics; taper when clinically appropriate.

drugs.dose_example: A common storm adjunct example is 2 mg every 6 hours; protocol varies.
drugs.role: Glucocorticoid adjunct reducing T4→T3 conversion.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Glucose/infection and steroid adverse effects.

drugs.dose_example: 4 g four times daily is a commonly described severe-thyrotoxicosis adjunct regimen; verify protocol.
drugs.role: Interrupts enterohepatic recycling of thyroid hormones.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: GI tolerance and spacing from other medicines because of absorption interactions.

drugs.dose_example: Specialist dosing is serum-level guided; no thyroid-specific universal fixed dose.
drugs.role: Can inhibit thyroid hormone release when conventional therapy is unsuitable.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Serum lithium, renal function, sodium and thyroid function.

drugs.dose_example: Specialist/region-specific dosing only; availability is limited and toxicity constrains use.
drugs.role: Blocks iodide uptake; occasionally used in iodine/amiodarone-related thyrotoxicosis in specialist settings.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: CBC and specialist toxicity monitoring.

drugs.dose_example: FDA regimen: 10 mg/kg first infusion then 20 mg/kg every 3 weeks for 7 additional infusions; verify current label/availability.
drugs.role: IGF-1R antibody for active thyroid eye disease in selected settings.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Glucose, hearing-related symptoms, infusion reactions; pregnancy avoidance per label.

drugs.dose_example: Pulse regimens are specialist-protocol specific; cumulative dose limits matter.
drugs.role: First-line immunosuppressive approach in many moderate-to-severe active orbitopathy protocols.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: Liver/cardiovascular/glucose/infection risk and cumulative steroid dose.

drugs.dose_example: Common DTC label dose 24 mg once daily; dose reductions are frequent.
drugs.role: VEGFR/FGFR/RET multikinase inhibition.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: BP, proteinuria, hepatic function and agent-specific toxicity; oncology supervision.

drugs.dose_example: 400 mg twice daily is the standard differentiated-thyroid-cancer label dose.
drugs.role: RAF/VEGFR multikinase inhibition.
drugs.monitoring_pearl: BP, proteinuria, hepatic function and agent-specific toxicity; oncology supervision.

drugs.dose_example: Common DTC tablet dose 60 mg once daily; verify indication/product-specific label.
drugs.role: MET/VEGFR/RET multikinase inhibition.
